business_requirements.title: Organisation goals and readiness profiles
business_requirements.need: Teams need a shared account of their goal, people, data and constraints.
business_requirements.acceptance: Authorised staff can save a named draft with sector, team size, goal, data readiness, experience and sensitive-data indicator; distinguish self-report from reviewed evidence.

business_requirements.title: Transparent readiness assessment
business_requirements.need: Teams need to choose a realistic first step.
business_requirements.acceptance: The same valid profile and rule version produce the same readiness stage, reasons, gaps and next steps; edits invalidate the prior assessment and no provider call is required.

business_requirements.title: Use cases and pilot selection
business_requirements.need: Teams need relevant tasks with explicit prerequisites and human responsibility.
business_requirements.acceptance: Each suggested use case names applicability, prerequisites, acceptance checks and human decision needs; an unsuitable or non-AI alternative can be shown without promising savings.

business_requirements.title: Evidence based tool discovery
business_requirements.need: Teams need a reliable starting point for finding AI tools.
business_requirements.acceptance: Every published tool names its provider, purpose, sources, review date and uncertainty; browsing does not imply approval, a quote or eligibility.

business_requirements.title: Comparable tools and offers
business_requirements.need: Teams need to understand differences before choosing a solution.
business_requirements.acceptance: Compare selected tools across common attributes, distinguish subscriptions from API access, and show missing costs or terms as unknown; do not manufacture a ranking.

business_requirements.title: Shared adoption plans
business_requirements.need: Teams need continuity across assessment, learning, procurement and pilots.
business_requirements.acceptance: Saved plans reopen with their brief, shortlist, progress and notes; edits preserve earlier revisions, stale updates conflict, and current access governs every read and retry.

business_requirements.title: Practical self paced learning
business_requirements.need: Staff need to practise safe and useful AI work.
business_requirements.acceptance: Lessons provide explanation, synthetic exercises and self-checks; self-recorded progress persists without being presented as competency certification.

business_requirements.title: Competency evidence
business_requirements.need: Organisations need evidence that staff can perform the intended task.
business_requirements.acceptance: A proposed assessment records a task rubric, submitted evidence, assessor decision and remediation; a completion checkbox alone cannot establish competence.

business_requirements.title: Learning programmes and cohorts
business_requirements.need: Teams need coordinated capacity building rather than isolated lessons.
business_requirements.acceptance: An authorised coordinator can assign a learning programme and review participation within organisation scope; learners see their own work and agreed sharing boundaries.

business_requirements.title: Consented AI advisory drafts
business_requirements.need: Teams need tailored advice while retaining human accountability.
business_requirements.acceptance: A separately permitted user explicitly consents to the submitted brief leaving the platform; the bounded draft remains unapproved, protected in storage and replayable without duplicate generation.

business_requirements.title: Human advisory cases
business_requirements.need: Teams need access to accountable human support for difficult adoption decisions.
business_requirements.acceptance: A case has a named adviser, agreed scope, disclosed conflict, restricted sharing, actions and recorded closure; advice alone cannot approve spending or disclose protected records.

business_requirements.title: AI task workbench
business_requirements.need: Teams need help applying AI to routine tasks using approved information.
business_requirements.acceptance: Approved templates define inputs, purpose, output checks and review ownership; generated work is visibly a draft and cannot execute consequential actions without an authorised human decision.

business_requirements.title: Procurement briefs
business_requirements.need: Buyers need a testable problem statement before approaching suppliers.
business_requirements.acceptance: An editable brief records requirements, permitted data, budget assumptions and supplier questions, retaining unknowns and avoiding invented prices or commitments.

business_requirements.title: Requests for offers and quotes
business_requirements.need: Buyers need comparable written offers.
business_requirements.acceptance: An authorised buyer can issue a versioned brief to named recipients after disclosure review; responses record currency, validity, inclusions, exclusions and evidence without sending messages automatically from a draft.

business_requirements.title: Total cost comparison
business_requirements.need: Buyers need to compare the full cost of alternatives.
business_requirements.acceptance: Comparison separates setup, recurring, usage, training, review, support and exit costs, states assumptions and dates, and excludes missing amounts from any asserted complete total.

business_requirements.title: Independent procurement decisions
business_requirements.need: Purchases need accountable approval and conflict controls.
business_requirements.acceptance: The requester cannot approve their own decision by the same natural person; the approver sees exact quote revisions, checks current authority and records the decision under the agreed procurement policy.

business_requirements.title: Supplier onboarding and publication
business_requirements.need: The marketplace needs attributable listings and evidence.
business_requirements.acceptance: Supplier submissions and supporting evidence remain private until independently reviewed; a published snapshot identifies verification scope, expiry and conflicts and does not imply blanket certification.

business_requirements.title: Marketplace neutrality and conflicts
business_requirements.need: Buyers need to understand how listings and advice may be influenced.
business_requirements.acceptance: Display the basis for placement, comparison and any commercial relationship; separate an editorial mapping from a verified capability or paid placement; revenue policy requires owner approval.

business_requirements.title: Bookings and service engagements
business_requirements.need: Buyers and advisers need a clear record of agreed work.
business_requirements.acceptance: A booking or engagement identifies parties, scope, terms, milestones and cancellation policy; external acceptance and delivery are recorded as evidence rather than inferred from an outbox intent.

business_requirements.title: Purchasing and payments
business_requirements.need: Some organisations may need transactions through the platform.
business_requirements.acceptance: Enable purchasing only after the owner chooses operator responsibility, financial controls and payment model; idempotency, reconciliation, refunds and independent approval must be qualified before money moves.

business_requirements.title: Pilot delivery and acceptance
business_requirements.need: Organisations need to move from a shortlist to a reviewed working pilot.
business_requirements.acceptance: Record the scope, success measure and actions; target delivery adds versioned milestones and independent acceptance evidence; self-recorded pilot checklists remain visibly different from accepted delivery.

business_requirements.title: Integration and deployment support
business_requirements.need: Teams need controlled connections to the tools they choose.
business_requirements.acceptance: Connections use reviewed scopes and server-side secrets, support revocation and failure visibility, and begin with synthetic trials; no integration can broaden data access or deploy from unapproved advice.

business_requirements.title: Usage budgets and spending controls
business_requirements.need: Organisations need to contain AI and service costs.
business_requirements.acceptance: Enforce configured tenant budgets before external generation, bound requests and timeouts, expose unavailable-credit conditions, and replay prior outcomes without automatically spending again.

business_requirements.title: Adoption outcomes
business_requirements.need: Teams need to know whether adoption improved their work.
business_requirements.acceptance: Record a baseline and outcome with time period, review effort, quality criteria and evidence; link to governed impact measurements where appropriate, retaining deterministic official arithmetic.

business_requirements.title: Organisation isolation and current access
business_requirements.need: Each organisation must control access to its own plans and cases.
business_requirements.acceptance: Cross-organisation selectors do not reveal protected content; reads, writes, replay, exports and disclosures recheck current scoped authority, and a platform operator gains no automatic business-data access.

business_requirements.title: Privacy and data lifecycle
business_requirements.need: Teams need explicit rules for information entered into AI or shared with suppliers.
business_requirements.acceptance: Show the allowed data boundary, obtain action-specific consent for disclosure, apply an approved retention policy and explain backup limitations; personal beneficiary data is excluded from the first pilot.

business_requirements.title: Revision history and accountable actions
business_requirements.need: Teams need a reliable history of who did what.
business_requirements.acceptance: Writes preserve immutable revisions and atomic audit, outbox and receipt records; identical retries replay an authorised original result and changed payloads conflict.

business_requirements.title: Accessible and understandable experience
business_requirements.need: Small nonprofit teams need a usable interface across devices and abilities.
business_requirements.acceptance: Critical journeys work by keyboard and on a narrow screen, with readable comparisons, clear labels and recoverable errors; automated findings and manual accessibility evidence are distinguished.

business_requirements.title: Reliable operation during dependency failure
business_requirements.need: Basic planning must continue when an AI provider is unavailable.
business_requirements.acceptance: Readiness, discovery, learning and saved drafts operate without AI generation; provider failure is explicit and bounded, ambiguous outcomes require safe retry or investigation, and no official data is corrupted.

business_requirements.title: Ownership and portability
business_requirements.need: Organisations need to retain their working information and exit a service.
business_requirements.acceptance: A separately permitted export includes approved scope, versions and context and is audited; export rights and provider exit obligations are stated before engagement.

business_requirements.title: Content maintenance and provenance
business_requirements.need: Tool and learning content can become outdated.
business_requirements.acceptance: Published content carries stable identifiers, versions, sources and review dates; material changes require review, retain prior meaning and mark unavailable or stale offers without rewriting saved history.

business_requirements.title: Support and incidents
business_requirements.need: Users need a clear route for help and harmful-output or access incidents.
business_requirements.acceptance: A support case records severity, owner, response expectation and restricted evidence; defined incidents can pause a connector or pilot, and resumption needs an accountable decision.

business_requirements.title: Governed release and onboarding
business_requirements.need: New features must reach organisations without bypassing their authority or operational checks.
business_requirements.acceptance: Release requires the four existing hosted jobs and owner confirmation; grants remain within reviewed ceilings, migrations are additive, and a deployment has an observable health result.

business_requirements.title: Feedback and improvement
business_requirements.need: The product needs evidence about usefulness and unmet needs.
business_requirements.acceptance: Capture optional task-level feedback with consent and minimised data; changes to rules, content or recommendations are reviewed and versioned rather than silently learned from private records.

business_requirements.title: Human control over consequential decisions
business_requirements.need: AI enablement must preserve responsibility for people, money and official results.
business_requirements.acceptance: Generated text, scores and checklists remain proposals; sensitive disclosures, purchases, deployment, eligibility and official impact calculations require the appropriate independent human or deterministic controls.

business_requirements.title: Reuse and interoperability
business_requirements.need: Delivery should accelerate through compatible existing components.
business_requirements.acceptance: Reuse the governed platform and compatible Mercy Corps and MSME patterns with provenance and licence records; preserve tenant isolation, independent approval and official calculation semantics.
